H: how do I know what percent contrast ratio it is

A: 
Contrast ratio (X:1) doesn't directly convert to a percentage — it's its own scale. But here are two ways to think about it:

**As a fraction of maximum possible contrast:**
The highest achievable contrast is 21:1 (pure black on pure white).
14.3 / 21 = **68% of maximum**

**Simple brightness difference** (a rougher formula some tools use):
(226 − 19) / 255 = 207 / 255 = **81%**

Neither is an official WCAG measurement — WCAG only uses the X:1 ratio. The industry convention is:

| Ratio | Informal reading |
|---|---|
| 21:1 | Perfect (100% of max) |
| 14:1 | Excellent (~68% of max) |
| 7:1 | Good — AAA |
| 4.5:1 | Acceptable — AA |
| 3:1 | Marginal — AA (large text only) |
| < 3:1 | Failing |

Your 14.3:1 is objectively excellent contrast. The readability issue you're seeing is not the colors — it's almost certainly the **10pt monospace font** being too small at your DPI. Try bumping to 12pt.

| % of max | Ratio | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| > 33% | > 7:1 | Great — WCAG AAA |
| 21–33% | 4.5–7:1 | Okay — WCAG AA |
| 14–21% | 3–4.5:1 | Marginal — large text only |
| < 14% | < 3:1 | Bad — fails everything |
